title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1969-02-12
lineage: SBD > Cassette Master > DAT > CD > EAC > shntool > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a blazing ’69 set featuring a smoking The Eleven, scorching Caution > Feedback and tight Alligator.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as crystal‑clear and well‑balanced, with only minor oversaturation noted by a few listeners. Musically the show is a fire‑storm – the Dark Star/​St. Stephen/​Eleven sequence ignites the night and the Caution > Feedback jam caps it off with heavy‑metal intensity, making this one of the standout ’69 performances.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 5 stars, highlighting both superb performance and excellent soundboard quality; consistency across many detailed comments yields a high confidence rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with strong instrument separation (noted especially on drums). A few reviewers mention slight oversaturation or minor muffling, but overall the fidelity is described as superb and well‑captured for a 45‑year‑old tape.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The early set builds momentum with a powerful Dark Star → St. Stephen → The Eleven sequence, then rolls into an incendiary Alligator and closes the first set with a blistering Caution > Feedback jam that carries high energy into the second set.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is repeatedly praised – roaring Fender Twin on The Eleven, "on fire" solos, heavy‑metal crunch at the end of Caution and soaring highs on Killer Dupree.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh receives glowing remarks for being "in all the right places", described as a harmony‑geometric genius and “bombing” with deep, resonant bass lines throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard work is highlighted in the feedback section – a low A note providing a cello‑like backbone and dynamic interaction with the guitars during Caution > Feedback.
band_member_comments.Drums: Listeners note clear separation of the two drummers (Bill & Mickey), indicating a tight, well‑mixed rhythm foundation.
